verdict.summary: Complete medium review of head 3376b878a15e3c6e04c4a26b90c79896cfa8bdf6 found two blocking correctness and acceptance-coverage gaps in exact-tree evidence handling.

blockingFindings.title: Changed-path tree lookup is not exact
blockingFindings.details: exactTreeEntries passes the changed path directly to recursive git ls-tree as a pathspec. Pathspecs select prefixes and patterns rather than one exact tree key. A valid file- or gitlink-to-directory change such as replacing `module` with `module/file` therefore returns descendants for the deleted `module` path and blocks as ambiguous. Paths containing pathspec metacharacters can similarly return unrelated entries or be mislabeled deleted. This violates the exact changed-tree evidence contract. Build an exact head path-to-entry map or combine literal lookup with diff status/mode evidence, and add regressions for file/gitlink-to-directory replacement and pathspec-like filenames.

blockingFindings.title: The admitted gitlink bound can exceed the prompt fact limit
blockingFindings.details: gitlinkManifestFromEntries admits up to 200 gitlinks, but gitlinkManifestFact concatenates the entire manifest into one verified fact. Prompt validation limits each verified fact to 4096 characters, while 200 even very short path/OID records exceed that limit by several times; one sufficiently long valid path can also exceed it. Such a manifest passes the new explicit bound and then fails prompt composition instead of being rendered for review. Bound the serialized representation consistently or split it into independently bounded facts, with boundary regressions proving the largest admitted manifest composes successfully.
